description:
Welcome to KISSAKOSMOS — a universe where forgotten objects find their voices!
We are creating an imaginative, animated storytelling experience that brings forgotten space objects to life. Through lovable characters, engaging narratives and interactive discoveries, we aim to take children and curious minds on an extraordinary journey through NASA's history of space exploration.
summary:
Our Project – An Interactive 3D Space Exploration Website

We are developing an interactive 3D website where users can explore the Moon and Mars and discover objects left behind by different space missions. Instead of just reading text or viewing pictures, users can explore these places through an interactive visual experience.

The website starts with an Explore page where users can choose between the Moon and Mars. After selecting a destination, they enter a 3D environment where they can rotate the planetary globe, move around and explore different locations.

The globe contains markers highlighting important 11 mission sites, including Apollo landing locations, lunar equipment, Mars rovers, landers and other scientific objects. By clicking on these markers, users can learn about each object's location, mission, purpose and history.

We are also adding animations to make the experience more engaging. These include spacecraft journey animations showing how missions travelled from Earth to the Moon or Mars. We are using 3D models from NASA resources and modifying some of them in Blender to create a more immersive experience.

Our goal is to bring planetary exploration, mission locations, 3D models, animations and historical information together in one place. Rather than simply reading about forgotten rovers or spacecraft, users can explore where they are and understand the stories behind them.
details:
1. Project Architecture and Structure

1.1 About Website

The website is divided into the following main sections:

  • Landing Page: The starting page where users can begin exploring and choose their destination.
  • Moon Exploration: An interactive 3D environment featuring lunar mission locations and abandoned equipment.
  • Mars Exploration:  3D environment where users can discover rover locations, landers and other mission objects(under development).
  • Object Information System: Displays details about selected objects, their missions, locations and historical importance.
  • Animation System: Shows selected spacecraft journeys from Earth to the Moon or Mars.
  • User Interface: Handles navigation, transitions, interactive text, visual effects and other website elements.

1.2 System Architecture

Frontend: HTML,CSS,React, Javascript 

Backend: No backend has been used.

3D Rendering: Taken Nasa’s listed resources and data to create 3D AR Rover and Moon.

2. Core Features and Implementation

2.1 Interactive Planetary Environments

Rather than presenting all the information as a conventional list or article, our project allows to :

1. Select the Moon or Mars.

2. Explore its (3D) three-dimensional surface.

3. Discover marked locations associated with space missions.

4. Select a location to learn about the equipment or mission.

5. View the available mission journey animation.

6. Understand the historical significance of the equipment and its place in space exploration.

Each location represents an opportunity to discover another part of humanity's exploration of space.

2.2 Mission Locations and Interactive Markers

Different markers are placed across the planetary surfaces to highlight important mission locations.  

  • Apollo landing sites and lunar exploration equipment.

2.3 Object Information and Mission Details and Timeline 

When users select a marker, they can view information related to that particular object or location.

The information includes:

  • Nasa’s Artifacts.
  • Mission associated with it.
  • Location on the Moon or Mars.
  • Its original purpose and historical importance.
  • Relevant images or 3D models backed by Nasa’s data.
  • The actual timing of the mission and artifacts.

Implementation of timeline : we have used NASA's resources and data to show exact timings of mission and landings.

2.4 Mission Journey Animations

  (under development) 

Selected spacecraft journeys from Earth to the Moon or Mars are represented through animations. This helps users understand how different missions reached their destinations.

2.5 User Interface and Interactive Design

Users can interact with artifacts and scroll timeline to know more about other mission and artifacts.

Include:

  • Navigation and page.
  • Animations and visuals.
  • Responsive design and accessibility.
  • Overall look and feel of the website.
3. Technologies, Tools and Resources

*FRONTEND: HTML,CSS,Javascript,React

*BACKEND: No backend was used.

*3D MODELLING: Blender

4.1 Development Workflow

Our development process was divided into the following stages:

  1. Planning: Selecting the challenge, developing the project idea and deciding the website structure.
  2. Design: Planning the landing page, planetary environments, navigation and overall user experience.
  3. Development: Building the frontend, 3D environments, information system and animations.
  4. Integration: Bringing the different components together, including 3D models and mission information.
  5. Testing: Checking navigation, interactions, 3D rendering, responsiveness and other features.
  6. Deployment: Publishing the website so it can be accessed for demonstration.

4.2 Team Contribution

5.2 Current Limitations

Although the project presents a very interesting and interactive way to connect with NASA's left equipment and the mission, it still has limitations that still exist in the current version of the project.

Some of them are following:

  • Availability and accuracy of historical mission information.
  • Limited coverage of abandoned objects and mission locations.
  • Level of detail and accuracy of 3D models.
  • Loading times and performance of 3D environments.
  • Compatibility with different devices and browsers.
  • Limitations in animation and planetary navigation.
  • Dependence on available external datasets and assets.
6. Future Scope – How Far Can This Project Go?

Our project can grow beyond a website that displays abandoned space equipment. With further development, it could become a larger platform for exploring the history of human space exploration.

6.1 Expanded Mission Database

The platform could include more abandoned and inactive equipment from different space missions, along with historical records, photographs, mission timelines and scientific information.

6.2 More Planetary Destinations

The exploration experience could expand beyond the Moon and Mars to other planetary bodies where human-made spacecraft and equipment have been left behind.

6.3 More Immersive 3D Experiences

Future versions could include more detailed planetary surfaces, realistic terrain, improved 3D models and additional exploration features. VR support could also be considered.

6.4 Interactive Mission Timelines

Users could explore individual missions through interactive timelines, covering everything from launch and landing to their operations and eventual completion.

6.5 Educational Integration

The platform could become a useful learning resource for schools, colleges and space enthusiasts. Instead of relying only on books or traditional reading, users could learn about space missions through interactive experiences.

Conclusion

Through this project, we aim to preserve and present an important part of human space exploration history using technology and interactive 3D experiences.

By bringing together planetary environments, mission locations, abandoned equipment, historical information and animations, we are creating another way for people to explore what humanity has left behind beyond Earth.

Although the current version focuses on the Moon and Mars, the same concept could eventually grow into a much larger archive of human space exploration.

Our goal is simple: the missions may be over, but their stories should never be forgotten.
